note:
ABANDONED INSTRUMENT, kept as evidence rather than deleted.

These are the first 6 runs (3 pairs) of docs/56's widened sweep. They are discarded because
the harness fence denied the agent an installed toolchain. `/root/.moon/bin/moon` exists and
is executable -- the MoonBit compiler is present in this container -- but `moon` is not on
PATH, so the only way to invoke it names a `/root/` path, and `src/gate.mjs`'s fence denies
anything naming `/home/` or `/root/` outside the sandbox.

In four of these six runs the agent diagnosed the problem correctly and ran the right fix --
export PATH="$PATH:/root/.moon/bin" && moon version, and once && moon test -p
mizchi/experimental_crypto/tls13 -- and the fence denied every one of them. 9 fence denials
across 6 runs, all naming /root/.moon.

5 of these 6 runs hit the 600 s cap, against 10 of 23 in docs/55. The rows are real agent
traffic and they are NOT the traffic of an agent doing the author's task: they are mostly an
agent trying to reach a compiler my own safety device was hiding.

They are not pooled with the corrected sweep. Two instruments in one record is the confound
the fence rule itself was kept uniform mid-sweep to avoid, and it would be no better for
being my own correction. The fence RULE is unchanged in the corrected sweep; only the
sandbox's PATH is, so that an installed toolchain can be invoked without naming a protected
path.
why: the fence hid an installed toolchain; the sandbox PATH was fixed and the sweep restarted from zero
